title: Implement percentile-decay adaptive canary and routing safeguard
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Added a percentile-decay adaptive canary detector and a traffic routing safeguard that can automatically redirect degraded traffic to warmed nodes or a slower but stable model variant. Backwards compatible config with opt-in rollout guard. Observability metrics and a short playbook included.
description: Motivation: existing canary detectors are sensitive to transient tail spikes and workload shifts, which leads to noisy alerts and unnecessary rollbacks. This PR introduces a percentile-decay detector that computes weighted percentiles with an exponential decay window to reduce sensitivity to short-lived spikes while preserving responsiveness to real regressions. It also adds a routing safeguard that limits rollout velocity when correlated infrastructure signals (queue depth, GPU-util, backpressure) are observed and optionally re-routes affected traffic to warmed nodes or pre-configured stable model variants. What changed: implemented detectors/percentile_decay_detector.py (core algorithm + configurable decay half-life + statistical significance test), added routing/traffic_safeguard.go (policy enforcement + actor that can instruct the router to split or reroute traffic), exported new telemetry: canary.percentile_decay{p50,p90,p95,p99}_weighted and canary.routing_safeguard_actions, updated telemetry/canary_metrics.promql with new alert rules, added tests/tests_percentile_decay.py covering synthetic workloads including steady drift and bursty tails, updated docs/canary_playbook.md with operational guidance and recovery steps, and CI pipeline changes to surface canary regression tickets. Config model: new canary config fields (decay_half_life_seconds, min_sample_count, effect_size_threshold, correlated_signal_threshold) are optional and default to conservative values so existing detectors behave unchanged. Backwards compatibility: no config changes required for existing canaries; the new detector can be selected explicitly or enabled via the global canary.policy field. Operational behavior: detector computes an exponentially weighted sample reservoir per route/model and evaluates p50/p90/p95 differences against a rolling baseline using a Studentized effect size. A significance filter avoids alerting on low-sample noisy routes. The routing safeguard subscribes to detector outputs and to infrastructure signals; when thresholds cross it gates traffic increases above a configured ramp and can move a percentage of traffic to warmed hosts or a pinned model variant until stability is restored. Tests and verification: unit tests for decay math and significance heuristics, integration test that runs a mini canary job against a simulated fleet (ci/integration/canary_simulator) to verify the routing actions under contention, and a smoke test that ensures metrics are emitted for dashboards. Impact and rollout: this PR is additive and feature-flagged behind canary.experimental.percentile_decay; we will enable it for perf-canary internal experiments for two weeks before wider rollout. Related work: complements ENG-9120 (batching fingerprinting) and SRE-1102 (backpressure alerting).
